newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarussian language advocates beaten, detained.
newsitem.headline: Belarussian language advocates beaten, detained.

text.p: At least four Belarussians were detained after scuffles with plain-clothes policemen on Thursday during a protest against the closure of the only Belarussian-language school in the capital Minsk.

Dozens of pupils protested against a July 1 decision by Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko, a strong advocate of the use of the Russian language, to confiscate the building for use by his own presidential administration.

Lukashenko, implementing pro-Moscow policies at home and facing criticism abroad for his authoritarian rule, unfailingly speaks Russian and once said: "It is impossible to express anything clever and intelligent in Belarussian."
The protesters, angry at Lukashenko's treatment of the former Soviet republic's native language, carried globes, maps, books and portraits of Belarussian writers.
Prior to independence in 1991 Belarus underwent centuries of domination from Moscow and pro-Russian language policies.
Deliberate russification under tsars and Soviet rulers left more than 90 per cent of its 10 million people speaking Russian, which is similar to but distinct from Belarussian.
Lukashenko, an ethnic Belarussian, has said there are "only two great languages in the world -- Russian and English".
More than 200 people have been jailed for short terms in Belarus for taking part in demonstrations opposing Lukashenko during the last two years.
